cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles, says it himself: "…the heavens opened and I saw visions of God." (Ezekiel 1:1) He doesn't say he heard about it from somebody else. He saw it with his own eyes, right there by the river.

The answer is fire, friends. Ezekiel sees "…a great cloud with fire flashing back and forth and brilliant light all around it." (Ezekiel 1:4) Back and forth, over and over, like it can't sit still. I've seen my oven act up, but never like that.

The answer is hands, friends. "Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands." (Ezekiel 1:8) That fits with the human form Ezekiel noticed when he first described them. All four living creatures had faces and wings too. Tucked under the wings on all four sides, that's a lot of hands.

The answer is False, friends. Ezekiel says, "They did not turn as they moved; each one went straight ahead." (Ezekiel 1:9) He says it again in verse 12. Everything about the way the living creatures move is straight ahead.

The other three faces are a lion, an ox and an eagle, friends. Each creature has a man's face, and also "…the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle." (Ezekiel 1:10) Four faces on one creature, just as verse 6 says. (Ezekiel 1:6)

The answer is wherever the spirit would go, friends. "Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 1:12) The living creatures don't wander off on their own. They go where the spirit goes.

The answer is as quick as flashes of lightning, friends. "The creatures were darting back and forth as quickly as flashes of lightning." (Ezekiel 1:14) Blink and you miss it. I can't even find my oven mitts that quickly.

The answer is a wheel, friends. Ezekiel says, "…I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces." (Ezekiel 1:15) One wheel for each living creature. And he's only getting started describing them.

The answer is True, friends. "As they moved, they went in any of the four directions, without pivoting as they moved." (Ezekiel 1:17) No turning around first, they just go. The living creatures don't turn as they move either. Each one goes straight ahead. (Ezekiel 1:9)
The answer is False, friends. The text says, "…when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose." (Ezekiel 1:19) Ezekiel says it again in verse 21. The wheels never stay behind.

The answer is that the spirit of the creatures is in the wheels, friends. The wheels rise alongside them "…because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels." (Ezekiel 1:20) So they move together because of that. Ezekiel gives that reason twice, in verses 20 and 21.

The answer is True, friends. "When they stood still, they lowered their wings." (Ezekiel 1:24) Moving, the wings sound like roaring waters. Standing still, they come down. Then a voice comes from above the expanse. (Ezekiel 1:25)

The answer is a throne, friends. "Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne with the appearance of sapphire…" (Ezekiel 1:26) Notice the words "likeness" and "appearance" in that verse. The throne sits above the expanse over the living creatures' heads.

The answer is a figure like that of a man, friends. Ezekiel sees "…on the throne high above was a figure like that of a man." (Ezekiel 1:26) Notice that he says the figure is "like" that of a man. He keeps that word "like" right there in the text. That throne is the one above the expanse, with the appearance of sapphire.

The answer is a rainbow, friends. "The appearance of the brilliant light all around Him was like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day." (Ezekiel 1:28) Ezekiel says this was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. Rainbow is my favorite color, so you know I'm glad it made the list.

The answer is that he falls facedown, friends. Ezekiel says, "…when I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking." (Ezekiel 1:28) I think it was a lot to take in. And in that same verse, he hears a voice speaking.
